verdict.rationale: Shopify documents a three-tier identification scheme (Token, Signed, Anonymous) for UCP traffic. The Signed tier uses RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures verified against the agent's published well-known UCP profile, and stronger tiers unlock higher rate limits and sensitive tools such as complete_checkout and Order MCP. A runtime probe confirmed that requests without a hosted agent profile are rejected with invalid_profile_url. Missing for 10: documentation of merchant-facing visibility or reporting that shows a store owner which tier or agent sent given traffic, and merchant-configurable policies per trust tier.

support.subject: As a merchant, agents identify themselves verifiably — registered profiles, signatures, or trust tiers — so I can tell trusted agent traffic from anonymous bots

citations.quote: UCP traffic to Shopify's MCP servers is classified into three tiers based on how your agent identifies itself
Stronger identification means higher rate limits and access to more sensitive tools.
Every request must include a `meta.ucp-agent.profile` URL pointing to your agent's UCP profile
returned the structured error invalid_profile_url, matching the documented requirement that agents identify themselves via a hosted profile before acting
Order MCP is available only to Token-tier agents.
